newsitem.title: UK: PowerGen rebounds as Bewag AG bid confirmed.
newsitem.headline: PowerGen rebounds as Bewag AG bid confirmed.

text.p: Shares in UK electricity generator PowerGen bounced back from an early fall on Wednesday, after the company confirmed it was considering bidding for German electricity supplier Berlin Kraft und Licht AG (Bewag).
At 1315 GMT the shares were up 1-1/2p at 574-1/2p in fairly active trade, having earlier dropped to a low of 549-1/2.

"We are assessing the commerical opportunities presented by the Bewag privatisation which are, potentially, very interesting. But no final decision has yet been taken as to whether we will bid," said PowerGen spokesman Mike Pollak.

A Financial Times (FT) report said PowerGen was thinking about making an offer for BEWAG -- due to be privatised early in 1997 -- but quoted Peter Hughes, director of PowerGen's overseas operations, as saying the deal was at a very early stage.
Analysts said the deal would be "an excellent move" if it went through, but one added: "It's a bit far off yet. PowerGen is one of 28 possible buyers, so it's at a very early stage."
The purchase would cost PowerGen 2.5 billion marks and would mark its first move into the area of electricity supply and distribution, the FT report said.
